newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes at lows, Brent trades up 34 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes at lows, Brent trades up 34 cts.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed at the lows on Friday after bearish news on Iraq took the steam out of short-covering, brokers said.

Front month July last traded 25 cents firmer at $162.75 a tonne, almost two dollars down from the session high of $164.50 achieved on the back of Brent firmness ahead of the expiry of the July front month.
August gas oil last traded 75 cents firmer at $164.50.
Front month July IPE Brent was 34 cents firmer at $17.78 a barrel at 1645 GMT.

"We came off after a headine about Iraq saying something like 'it was ready to resume exports, but', and the 'but' was enough to take the heat out of things," a gas oil trader said. "So we are back to the nervous market we had a few days ago."

In New York, Iraqi Ambassador to the U.N. Nizar Hamdoon said Baghdad had no interest in delaying renewed oil sales under the recently extended "oil-for-food" accord, but would not export more oil until an effective aid distribution plan was in place.
"No, we have no interest in delaying the sales. But, we want this deal to not only be oil for money, but oil for food and medicine," said Hamdoon.
"We want to be assured on food and medicine distribution."

Iraq is permitted to sell $2.14 billion worth of crude over a 180-day period, in order to buy food, medicine and supplies outlawed by broad sanctions slapped on Baghdad after its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
Traders said gas oil was dull in sympathy with a moribund physical market quietened by the expiry of June.
"There has been relatively little volume so it has been a non-event in terms of trading," a trader said.
"A lot will depend on where Brent closes tonight. It should give strong direction for the next week.
"Things look steady for now but anything can happen shortly before the close," he said.
Brent crude futures earlier had held onto gains after NYMEX opened on Friday, buoyed by short covering ahead of the expiry of the July Brent contract.
With the NYMEX July crude options contract expiring today there was additional buying support in the market, said brokers.
July New York crude futures were 20 cents higher at $18.89 a barrel at 1645 GMT.
